summary: Bloomington sits on the flat, sun-baked alluvial plain between the San Bernardino Mountains to the north and the Jurupa Hills to the south, and that geography defines daily life more than any single statistic: with an annual average daytime high of 78°F and nearly 9.7 hours of sunshine per day, shade and air conditioning are not luxuries but utilities. This unincorporated census-designated place — technically governed by San Bernardino County, not its own city hall — occupies just 6.1 square miles wedged between Fontana and Loma Linda along the I-10 corridor, making it functionally a logistics and distribution bedroom community where warehouses and residential blocks alternate without much buffer. A median home value of $443,300 against a median household income of $81,220 yields a price-to-income ratio around 5.5×, which is strained but notably less brutal than coastal Southern California; median rent at $1,555 consumes roughly 23% of that median gross income, a somewhat manageable figure. The tradeoff is connectivity: employment clusters in warehousing, healthcare (Loma Linda University Medical Center is minutes east), and freight mean most jobs are reachable without a brutal commute, but the street grid is fragmented by rail lines and freeway infrastructure, making errands feel car-dependent even across short distances. Bloomington is a place where affordable square footage and Inland Empire job access come packaged with industrial adjacency and limited walkable public space — a calculus that pencils out differently depending on where your paycheck originates.
